Hi @Candelaria Justiniano ,

Thank you for reaching out.

Azure OpenAI Service pricing is managed independently from OpenAI's public pricing announcements. As a result, price changes announced by OpenAI may not be reflected immediately, or at the same time, in Azure. Azure pricing updates are communicated through the official Azure pricing pages and service documentation when they become available.

At this time, we do not have information regarding any upcoming pricing changes or estimated timelines for GPT-5.6 Luna/Terra pricing updates in Azure. 

For the most current Azure OpenAI pricing information, please refer to the Azure pricing documentation and announcements.

We appreciate your feedback and understand the importance of pricing transparency when planning workloads. If there are any official updates, they will be communicated through Microsoft’s standard channels.

results.title: Several Microsoft Foundry Issues - Cache, open-source, pricing - Microsoft Q&A
highlights:
#### Pricing not updated

For every price change the main providers do, we have to wait for a long time to see that change reflected on our bills. While GPT 5.6 Luna price reductions happened the 30th of July we are still being billed the old pricing. Some examples of people complaining.

- https://www.reddit.com/r/AZURE/comments/1vkrsj0/price_of_gpt56luna/
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5972276/pricing-gpt-5-6-luna-modle

The main Microsoft blog mentions the prices are updated https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/gpt-5-6-now-available-in-microsoft-foundry/ but they are neither reflected on the Azure Foundry pricing page https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/azure-openai/ nor our bills. 

Why is this taking so long ? All other AI providers updated this in no more than 1 day...

...

3. Pricing and billing

The GPT-5.6 announcement published pricing for Sol, Terra, and Luna models and states that the models are generally available in Microsoft Foundry. [GPT-5.6 no...ion agents | Azure.Microsoft.com]

However, differences between an announcement, the public pricing page, and an individual customer's invoice cannot be diagnosed from a forum post alone. Microsoft documentation states that billing details are available through Cost Management + Billing and are not shown directly in the Foundry portal.

If usage that occurred after a pricing change appears to have been charged at a previous rate, the correct action is to open a billing support case and provide:

- Subscription ID
- Billing account or enrollment information
- Deployment type
- Azure region
- Usage dates
- Meter details
- Expected versus observed charges

This enables the billing team to investigate the specific metering records.

Hi Tushaar V ,

Thank you for raising this question.

OpenAI price changes and Azure OpenAI pricing updates are managed separately. When OpenAI announces a price reduction, it may take some time before the corresponding Azure pricing pages and billing meters are updated across Azure regions and commercial agreements.

The authoritative source for Azure OpenAI pricing is the Azure pricing page. Once pricing updates are officially rolled out in Azure, the updated rates will be reflected there and applied according to Azure's billing policies.

If you would like confirmation on the status of a specific GPT‑5.6 pricing update, please share us in the Private message.

...

Hi @Tushaar V 

Pricing updates on the public Azure OpenAI Pricing page lag direct OpenAI announcements due to Azure's enterprise billing table deployment cycle across Enterprise Agreements (EA) and Microsoft Customer Agreements (MCA).

Key things to know:

1. Billing Cycle Updates: Azure updates price meters on standard monthly billing synchronization cadences.
2. Enterprise Features Included: Azure OpenAI rates cover enterprise SLA commitments, VNet private endpoints, customer-managed keys (CMK), and regional compliance guarantees.
3. Automatic Adjustment: Once updated meters publish, rate reductions automatically apply to your deployment usage meters without requiring model redeployment.

Ref: Azure OpenAI Service Pricing Details

results.title: Azure overcharged us by $80K, how can we get a refund? - Microsoft Q&A
highlights:
The team has completed their investigation and identified a service configuration issue that impacted billing for some customers using GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Terra, and GPT-5.6 Luna deployments.

Impact Period: July 9, 2026, 18:00 UTC – July 22, 2026, 18:44 UTC

During this period, a configuration error caused some usage to be mapped to incorrect billing meters, which may have resulted in higher-than-expected charges.

The OpenAI team has confirmed that:

- The configuration issue has been corrected.
- The fix was fully deployed by July 22, 2026.
- Billing for affected deployments is now operating as intended.
- No action is required from customers at this time.

results.title: Separate Billing when free credits are available. - Microsoft Q&A
highlights:
The $200 credit is automatically applied to eligible Azure services during the free trial period. However, charges can still appear if certain services are not included in the free offer or if usage exceeds the free limits

...

The supported reasons are:

1. The $200 credit applies only during the first 30 days of a new Azure free account. During that period, charges for eligible Azure services are deducted from the credit balance.
2. Not all offerings are covered by Azure credits. Separate billing can happen for: 

- Partner-provided or non-Microsoft Marketplace products
- Azure support plans
- Software subscriptions or licenses not billed as Azure consumption
- For sponsorship scenarios, some entitlement-based purchases such as reserved instances or savings plans
3. Third-party Marketplace services are billed separately. Free credits can’t be applied to external services, so those charges can appear in addition to normal Azure usage.
4. If the free-account credit is exhausted or expired, charges continue at pay-as-you-go rates. Azure free account invoices are created when the monthly credit amount is exceeded.

results.title: Unbilled Pricing Discrepancy & Refund Request: DeepSeek V4 Flash "Cached Global Tokens" Charged at ~357x Published Rate - Microsoft Q&A
highlights:
Environment Details:

- Service: Azure AI Foundry (Serverless)

Model: DeepSeek V4 Flash

Deployment Dates: June 6–7, 2026

Subscription Billing Impact: ₹161,648.62 (~$1,900 USD)

### Issue Context

During a two-day deployment of DeepSeek V4 Flash via Azure AI Foundry, our subscription incurred an unexpected charge of ₹161,648.62, with 98.4% of the total cost (₹158,990.13 / ~$1,684.33) originating from a single line item: "V4 Flash Cached Global Tokens".

When checking with Azure Support, we were informed that the usage report reflects an effective applied rate of $0.01 per K ($10.00 per 1M tokens) for cached tokens. Support advised us to post here on Microsoft Q&A for model-specific billing and pricing clarification.

### The Discrepancy

We verified the math behind our invoice, but the applied cached token rate contradicts Microsoft's published pricing:

Input Tokens: 145,840.449K @ ~₹17.93/M ($0.19/M) = ₹2,615.62 (Verified & Matches Published Documentation)

Output Tokens: 890.597K @ ~₹48.14/M ($0.51/M) = ₹42.87 (Verified & Matches Published Documentation)

Cached Global Tokens: 168,432.896K @ $0.01 per K ($10.00 / 1M tokens) = ₹158,990.13 (~$1,684.33) (Major Discrepancy)

#### Comparison with Published Microsoft Documentation:

According to official Microsoft Tech Community documentation (Introducing DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro in Microsoft Foundry), the official rates are:

Input: $0.19 / 1M tokens

Output: $0.51 / 1M tokens

Cached Input: $0.028 / 1M tokens

The rate applied to our deployment ($10.00 / 1M tokens) is ~357× higher than Microsoft's officially published $0.028 / 1M tokens rate for Cached Input on DeepSeek V4 Flash.
